HUTCHEON & PEARCE
Location: DUBBO / WARREN, NSW
Employment Type: FULL-TIME PERMANENT

Automotive Electrician
Salary: $80,000 to $85,000 per annum

Diesel Motor Mechanic
Salary: $80,000 to $95,000 per annum

Job Ad Start Date: 20/07/26
Job Ad Finish Date: 19/08/26

About Hutcheon and Pearce Hutcheon & Pearce has always been a proud family business. To us, our team is family. Since 1953, we have grown to more than560 people across 20 branches in NSW. As we continue to grow alongside the needs of our customers in the ever-changing agricultural sector, it's important that we find the best people to join our team. We are seeking qualified and motivated trade professionals to join our Service team. These roles involve diagnostics, repairs, servicing and maintenance of agricultural, turf and diesel-powered equipment, including electrical, electronic, hydraulic and mechanical systems.

Automotive Electrician

Duties and Responsibilities

- Diagnose electrical and electronic faults using test equipment and diagnostic tools.
- Repair and replace faulty wiring, ignition systems, alternators, starter motors, voltage regulators, fuses, lamps and switches.
- Install and connect electrical equipment, electronic components and power-operated accessories.
- Adjust engine control systems and timing.
- Carry out servicing and maintenance on agricultural and turf equipment.
- Complete service reports, timesheets and related documentation.
- Maintain tools, equipment and a safe, clean work area.

Qualifications

- AQF Certificate III including at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV (ANZSCO Skill Level 3) or
similar.
- At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications listed above.

Skills and Experience

- Experience in diagnosing and repairing automotive electrical and electronic systems.
- Ability to use test equipment and diagnostic tools to identify electrical faults.
- Ability to install, maintain and repair electrical wiring and electronic components.
- Ability to perform repairs and maintenance using technical manuals, special tools and manufacturer procedures.
- Basic computer skills, including the ability to use Service Advisor or similar systems.
- Good fault-finding, communication and safety awareness.
- Current driver's licence required; forklift licence preferred.
- Comprehensive trade tool kit required.

Diesel Motor Mechanics

Duties and Responsibilities

- Perform diagnostics, repairs, servicing and maintenance on agricultural and turf equipment.
- Inspect and repair diesel engines and associated mechanical, hydraulic and electrical systems.
- Carry out scheduled servicing using technical manuals and specialised tools.
- Operate vehicles and equipment for testing and diagnostic purposes.
- Complete service documentation and maintain tools, vehicles and workshop equipment.
- Follow workplace safety procedures and company policies.

Qualifications

- AQF Certificate III including at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV (ANZSCO Skill Level 3) or similar.
- At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications listed above.

Skills and Experience

- Experience in diesel engine repairs and equipment maintenance.
- Proficient knowledge of mechanical, electrical and hydraulic systems used in the repair of agricultural, turf, plant or similar equipment.
- Ability to perform repairs and required maintenance using special tools and equipment in accordance with technical manuals and manufacturer procedures.
- Ability to use diagnostic tools, service manuals and basic computer systems.
- Ability to use Service Advisor and other basic computer functions.
- Good troubleshooting, communication and safety awareness.
- Current driver's licence required; forklift licence preferred.
- Comprehensive trade tool kit required.

Key Performance Indicators

- Meet productivity and quality targets.
- Complete repairs within allocated timeframes.
- Maintain safe work practices and compliance with company procedures.
- Deliver reliable workmanship and good customer service.

Job description:

 
Client Services Officers coordinate client referrals, assessments, and support plan reviews, ensuring services remain appropriate, compliant, and responsive to client needs. They also maintain accurate records, support staff training and onboarding, manage client concerns, and contribute to quality, safety, and continuous improvement initiatives.

 

 






 

The Team

Home Care South is a dynamic and client-focused team within the Department of Health (Tasmania), dedicated to delivering high-quality in-home support services across Southern Tasmania. Our primary mission is to support frail older people and younger people with disabilities to remain safely and independently in their homes and communities, in line with the Charter of Aged Care Rights and the Aged Care Quality Standards.

Our team operates as a critical link between clients, families, care providers, and the wider health system. Client Services Officers (CSOs) form the backbone of Home Care South, working autonomously while travelling across the region to ensure service quality, conduct assessments, support field staff, and respond to individual client needs.

The Role

Client Services Officers work with a high degree of independence and are regularly required to travel throughout Southern Tasmania. The Client Services Officer reports directly to the Manager, Home Care South and is responsible for:

Coordinating new referrals and home care assessments for incoming and re-engaging clients.

Reassessing support plans to ensure services remain appropriate, responsive, and compliant with statutory obligations.

Maintaining accurate and up-to-date client databases and documentation for reporting and quality assurance.

Investigating and resolving client concerns independently to uphold service quality and accountability.

Leading the onboarding, orientation, and ongoing training of field staff to maintain high standards of care delivery.

Driving continuous improvement by contributing to quality and safety initiatives and maintaining Work Health & Safety compliance.

You will need

Demonstrated ability to contribute effectively to the development and continuing improvement of services provided to clients.

Demonstrated ability to assist with the design and delivery of training programs for new and existing staff.

Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make independent and collaborative judgments as well as implement management decisions.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment

Permanent part time, day worker position, working 30.4 hours per fortnight, commencing as soon as possible.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$76,849 to $82,996 per annum (Pro rata). Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with Public Sector Unions Wages Agreement 2025.

Salary Packaging

You'll have access to salary package a range of benefits including living expenses up to $9,010 + $2,650 in meal entertainment each FBT year + other benefits if eligible. 

Benefits available to eligible candidates

Professional development and accelerated pathways.

A range of leave entitlements, including study leave and Professional Development Support.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Certificate Level III in Individual Support or a related qualification and a demonstrated willingness to increase knowledge and skills.

Current Driver's Licence
